The recommendation

Who should choose ntopng

ntopng is for network and security teams that want one web interface for real-time and historical traffic visibility. It reads packets from a mirror port or TAP, flows from NetFlow and sFlow exporters (through nProbe), SNMP devices, firewall logs and IDS events. Choose it when you want to see who talks to whom, with which application, and how well, without stitching several tools together.

  • You need live and historical views of hosts, flows, applications, ASes and countries.
  • You want alerts and behavioral checks, plus SNMP, active monitoring and SLA reporting in the same tool.
  • You want to start free: the Community edition is open source (GPLv3), Pro and Enterprise add features and capacity.

The ideal use case

Ideal use case for ntopng

  • Environment: enterprise or service provider networks, from a small office to large uplinks. Runs on Linux, FreeBSD, Windows x64, macOS and Raspberry Pi OS.
  • Team: network administrators and security operations that read dashboards daily and integrate through the REST API.
  • Technical requirements: a mirror port or TAP, or flow exporters feeding nProbe. Small networks need 2 cores and 2 GB RAM, 10 Gbps and above need 8+ cores and 16+ GB.
  • Problem solved: find top talkers, latency, TCP retransmissions, VoIP quality and suspicious behavior, then keep the history for reports and post-mortem analysis.

Ideal for Every Environment

Deployment scenarios

Flow Collection in Enterprise Networks

Monitor hundreds of thousands of hosts with zero‑delay traffic analysis on high‑speed uplinks.
Flow collection requires ntopng to be used in conjunction with nProbe which can act as probe/proxy.
The communication between nProbe and ntopng takes place over ZeroMQ, a publish-subscribe protocol that allows ntopng to communicate with nProbe.
A remote nProbe is physically monitoring a mirror from a NIC and sending monitored flows to ntopng, or is collecting NetFlow v5/v9/IPFIX or sFlow from one or more exporters (routers or switches). nProbe Cento allows you to monitor even 100 Gbit links when processing packets from a mirror port, yet providing application protocol information by running nDPI.

Capture Packets from a Mirror/TAP

Mirror (SPAN) ports or TAP devices allow network monitoring tools to observe all packets flowing through the network for for network visibility, troubleshooting, threat detection, and capacity planning, without generating traffic or altering the data path.

  • Mirror Port (SPAN): available on most managed switches, duplicates traffic from selected ports or VLANs to a dedicated monitoring port.
  • TAP Device: transparently copies all network traffic at the physical layer, acting as a bump-in-the-wire and providing a fail-safe method for capturing traffic.

A physical NIC card connected to a mirror can be monitored by ntopng itself by simply specifying its interface name. This configuration can be used to monitor a mirror port from a switch, or in conjunction with a TAP device by aggregating two directions from two network interfaces. Alternatively, it is possible to use ntopng in combination with nProbe or nProbe Cento to scale up to 100 Gbit.

IDS Integration and Security Operations

Combine L7 visibility, IDS integration, syslog ingestion and alerts for full awareness. ntopng, in addition to behavioral checks able to detect traffic anomalies, can ingest events from IDS systems like Suricata enriching traffic analytics with security insights for faster threat detection and response.

The alternatives

ntopng alternatives, compared

Same criteria for each option: role, when to choose it, limits and cost.

ntopng with nProbe
  • Role: Flow collection from routers and switches (NetFlow v5/v9/IPFIX, sFlow) over ZeroMQ.
  • Choose it when: You have many exporters or remote sites and no packet access.
  • Limits: Flows carry less detail than packets. One more component to run.
  • Cost: nProbe Pro 299.95 euro, Enterprise S from 499.95 euro.
ntopng with nProbe Cento
  • Role: Packet analysis of 1, 10, 40 and 100 Gbit links, classified with nDPI.
  • Choose it when: You monitor links up to 100 Gbit from a mirror port.
  • Limits: Needs capable hardware; ntopng alone captures with libpcap or PF_RING.
  • Cost: Cento from 499.95 euro.
ntopng Community, Pro and Enterprise
  • Role: Same product, three editions.
  • Choose it when: Community for home and practitioners, Pro for offices and small enterprises, Enterprise for large organisations and ISPs.
  • Limits: Community is for small networks; historical data and reports, extended SNMP and identity management are Enterprise features.
  • Cost: Community free, Pro 299.95 euro, Enterprise M 699.95 euro, L 899.95 euro, XL 1,499.95 euro.

The tradeoffs

When ntopng is not the right choice

  • ntopng is not a packet recorder. To keep full packets for forensics, add n2disk.
  • It does not collect NetFlow or sFlow alone: add nProbe as probe and proxy.
  • It detects and alerts. For inline policy enforcement see nEdge.
  • Large networks (10 Gbps and above) need 8+ cores and 16+ GB RAM, and the Enterprise edition for historical data and reports.

The proof

Specifications, versions, pricing and documentation

Features, supported platforms and protocols, editions with prices, documentation links and answers to common questions follow below.

at a glance

Key Features

  • Realtime network traffic, active flows and hosts
  • Top talkers, AS, L7 application protocols, categories
  • Protocol and application detection powered by nDPI
  • Custom reports on historical data with metrics and trends
  • Application latencies, Round Trip Time (RTT), throughput
  • TCP metrics including retransmissions, out of order, packet loss
  • Multimedia and VoIP metrics including jitter, MOS
  • Hosts geolocalisation
  • Multi‑interface support: mirror, TAP, flow collection
  • Packet capture via libpcap and PF_RING
  • Flow collection from nProbe, NetFlow and sFlow exporters
  • HTML5 web user interface
  • REST API to ease integrations with third-parties
  • Full Layer-2 support and statistics
  • Tunnel decapsulation including GTP andGRE
  • Export to ElasticSearch and bigdata systems
  • Interactive exploration of historical data exported (ClickHouse)
  • Behavioural checks and alert notifications
  • SNMP v1/v2c/v3 support
  • Identity Management and VPN correlation
  • Native nTap support for remote capture on cloud, VMs, containers
  • Active monitoring and SLA reporting

Works great with nProbe!

ntopng works even better in distributed networks or high-speed links when paired with nProbe or nProbe Cento!

FAQ

Frequently Asked Questions

How much does ntopng cost?

The Community edition is free. ntopng Pro costs 299.95 euro, Enterprise M 699.95 euro, Enterprise L 899.95 euro and Enterprise XL 1,499.95 euro. Licenses are perpetual and include one year of maintenance, updates and support. See the pricing page.

Is ntopng free?

The Community edition of ntopng is free and open source under the GNU GPLv3 license. Professional and Enterprise editions are commercial, see the pricing page.

Which operating systems does ntopng support?

ntopng runs on Linux, FreeBSD, Windows x64 (including Windows 10 and 11), macOS and Raspberry Pi OS.

Do I need nProbe to use ntopng?

No. ntopng captures traffic from mirror ports and TAPs with libpcap or PF_RING. To collect NetFlow and sFlow from routers and switches, use nProbe as probe and proxy.

How does ntopng know the application behind a flow?

ntopng uses nDPI, the ntop deep packet inspection library, to detect hundreds of Layer-7 protocols, including encrypted traffic.
